project.description:
Japanese HR and payroll administration, and the scale test of this repository: eight Souther modules under src/main/souther, compiled together in one build, with an import chain five deep. example.employee holds the vocabulary the other seven speak; example.dependents decides who is a dependant, under the two different definitions the social-insurance system and the income-tax system each hold; example.socialinsurance the health and pension coverage, the fifty-grade standard monthly remuneration table and the three ways a grade is decided; example.employmentinsurance the unemployment-insurance coverage and the separation reasons; example.attendance working hours, the overtime premium rates and annual leave; example.payroll gross to net; example.yearendadjustment the year-end reconciliation of withheld tax; and example.filing the workflow a notification goes through on its way to the authorities.
The rules are the ones Japanese labour and social-insurance law actually enforces — the 130万-yen dependant ceiling, the twenty-hour employment-insurance threshold, the two-grade difference an occasional revision needs, the eight-tenths attendance rate annual leave needs, and the spouse deduction's two-axis income matrix. Each threshold carries a Why comment saying what it is for, so a reader can tell a rule that may be changed from one that may not.
The boundary is one JUnit smoke test per module and nothing else: no Spring, no jOOQ, no database, no REST. Where the language could not state a rule directly, the file says so at the declaration that hit it, and the README's dogfooding findings collect them.
